dialect.detail: JMA ORCA medical receipt software (open-cobol/GnuCOBOL); comment references 'open-cobol 0.23' adaptation in 2005
evidence: SELECT ... ASSIGN RECEERR without DD: syntax

purpose.domain_detail: JMA ORCA standard medical receipt (Nissho) software — monthly outpatient billing summary report
purpose.summary: This program is part of the JMA ORCA medical receipt system. It processes monthly outpatient visit data, aggregating billing amounts, insurance combinations, self-pay items, and subsidy amounts for a monthly summary report. It handles multiple insurance types, re-examination counts, consumption tax calculations, and deposit/payment reconciliation.

notable_features: 44 COPY statements referencing ORCA-specific copybooks (A00000D123.INC, A00000D1231.INC, CPCOMMONSHELL.INC, CPERRFL.INC)
142 CALL statements indicating heavy use of subprogram library
INDEXED file organization with DYNAMIC access
Japanese-language comments (EUC-JP encoded, decoded as latin-1)
No COMP-3 usage (unusual for financial COBOL)
No EXEC SQL or EXEC CICS
Program option support via INI file (later removed 2009/04/16)
OCCURS clause for self-pay item arrays
verdict.notes: File decoded as latin-1 but comments are actually EUC-JP encoded Japanese text, appearing as mojibake. Source is clearly the JMA ORCA open-source medical receipt system, a well-known Japanese healthcare COBOL application targeting GnuCOBOL (formerly open-cobol). The 46% comment ratio reflects extensive Japanese-language inline documentation and change history. No COMP-3 is notable for a financial application but consistent with ORCA codebase style.
